prize_parts.citation: for showing how differences between firms and their selection into exporting shape trade patterns, reallocation and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My preferred part is unchanged: one achievement, B048, credited to Melitz and Helpman. The reasons are the same as in round 1, and the exchange has sharpened them. The test I apply across fields is whether the work changed what we know and how we know it. Firm heterogeneity moved the unit of analysis in trade from the industry to the firm. It identified a distinct channel for the gains from trade, namely selection and reallocation toward more productive firms. It also made firm-level micro data the standard place where trade theory meets evidence. Its qualitative predictions (selection into exporting, exporter premia, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been checked in many countries over more than twenty years, so the maturity question is largely settled. As an economic historian, I find a mechanism that can be confronted with archival and administrative micro data more persuasive than one whose central causal reading depends on coarse country-level proxies. Melitz (2003) is the identifiable core, and Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, together with his earlier trade theory, makes the two-name credit coherent. I have considered the chair's question on the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum priority issue. A citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade framework would be sufficient, because it does not claim the empirical firm-level facts as the laureates' own. That wording is the one I propose. My configuration has not changed. What has changed is the reasoning behind my alternatives. Reading the other round-1 files, I am more convinced that B001 is the main contest, so I now list it first among the alternatives. B049 becomes the second alternative because of the overlap and identification concerns that Andersson and I both raised.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum developed closely parallel firm-level facts and models, and none is on this ballot entry. A Melitz-Helpman prize could therefore be read as favouring the theory over the empirical foundations. Hjalmarsson is right that this is a priority question and not just a later extension, and a three-name cap cannot resolve it. Welfare-gain magnitudes also depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity, so the discovery is the qualitative mechanism and not a measured size of the gains. Helpman also appears in another candidate package (B026), which may affect how the citation is framed. If the committee gives weight to the 2008 trade prize, B048 could be disadvantaged, but that is a question of timing and not of merit. I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not independently verified any source.

responses.point: Hassler, the chair, ranks B001 slightly ahead of B048 because he finds the creation of a new field somewhat more decisive than refinement within an established one. He would word the citation around measurable institutions and investor protection and not around legal origin as a proven cause. He calls the gap with B048 small.
responses.response: I take the wording seriously. A citation that rests on the data and on the regularity that investor protection and enforcement can be measured and relate to financial outcomes avoids the weakest part of the thesis. It still leaves two problems for me. First, what is credited would then be mainly the research design and descriptive regularities, and the question of why those regularities arise, which gave the programme its explanatory ambition, would stay open. For a historian that open question is the heart of the matter, because legal origin may proxy for colonial and institutional history. Second, the Vishny exclusion remains, and you concede it is a real cost. Head to head, I would still put B048 first, because its credited mechanism has been tested against micro-data and the cap costs it less. What would move me toward B001 is a showing that its established regularities, taken apart from the causal reading, are robust to alternative coding of legal rules. I have not seen that shown in this exchange. I also note that you are the chair and a B001 supporter, and I treat your wording proposal as a substantive argument, not as procedure.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B001 first and argues that the identification critiques qualify the mechanism more than they undermine the discovery. He says a prize can recognise the founding of a field even if its first causal story is only partly right. He lists B049 and B048 as alternatives.
responses.response: I agree that field-founding is a legitimate ground for a prize, and I do not dismiss B001. I rank it as my first alternative. My difference is about how much of the discovery stays standing if the causal story is set aside. If the lasting contribution is the cross-country facts and the research design, then the citation honours data construction, and the measurement and coding critiques bear directly on exactly that contribution, not only on the interpretation. In B048 the contested part is the size of welfare gains, while the mechanism and its qualitative predictions are not seriously disputed. I would also not rest the comparison on conduct controversies, which none of us can assess from the evidence supplied. I would treat B001 as the strongest rival to B048, and I would accept it as a credible outcome if the committee puts field creation ahead of robustness.

responses.point: Andersson, my Lund colleague, ranked B049 first in his opening but now puts B048 first. He says he hesitates over B049 because a Persson-Tabellini prize would rest on contested cross-country constitutional identification and because of thematic overlap with the 2024 prize. He keeps B049 as his first alternative.
responses.response: We reached similar conclusions from different starting points, and I want to be clear that this is independent reasoning and not coordination between Lund colleagues. In round 1 I named B049 as my first alternative. After reading the exchange, I give it less weight than B001, for the reasons you give. The identification of effects of electoral rules and constitutions from cross-country variation is contested, and I still do not know whether the committee sees the constitutions work and Besley's state-capacity work as one achievement or two. I differ slightly on overlap with 2024. I would treat it as a reduction in marginal novelty and not as a ground for disqualifying the work, and I would not let it substitute for evidence about the work itself. B049 remains my second alternative, since its foundational standing is clear. It trails B001 for me mainly on the unresolved one-versus-two achievement question.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B048 first and calls the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum issue the real vulnerability, because it concerns priority on the empirical foundations and not just a later extension. She proposes drafting the citation around the selection mechanism and gains-from-trade framework so that it does not overclaim the firm-level facts.
responses.response: I agree, and I adopt that drafting in my citation. It states what the two laureates are credited with, the model of selection and reallocation and its extension to exporting versus FDI, and it makes no claim to the empirical firm-level facts as a whole. I would add that the wording cannot remove the priority issue, and the committee should say so openly in deliberation and not treat the wording as a fix. If a majority judged the priority question so material that the empirical foundations must be credited together with the theory, B048 would no longer fit a two-name configuration within the three-person cap. I regard that as a real risk, but not one that changes the order for me now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum priority question as material enough to require crediting the empirical foundations, which the ballot entry and the three-person cap cannot accommodate.
How much of Helpman's claim on B048 is affected by his appearance in B026, and whether the committee will treat that as a framing issue or as an unresolved competing claim.
How sensitive the welfare-gain conclusions are to functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity, and whether this weakens the claim of a robust discovery.

Whether the factual regularities in B001 survive alternative coding of legal rules independently of the causal reading. I have not seen that shown, and it is the main thing that could raise B001 above B048 for me.
Whether B049 is one achievement or two, and how much thematic overlap with the 2024 institutions prize should count as reduced marginal novelty.

My assessments rest on my own knowledge of the literature and have not been independently verified. The simulation also treats every member's vote as a modelling assumption, and this is not a claim about actual proceedings.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Melitz or Helpman is apparent from my supplied profile, and none to the credited names of B001 or B049, my alternatives. My field of economic history and regional growth is adjacent to Redding's spatial and quantitative work. That is research proximity and not a personal tie, and I have kept him out of my credit. Tommy Andersson, a committee colleague at Lund, appears in this exchange as a B049 proponent who has moved to B048, and I disclose the shared affiliation. I reached my own position independently of him. Jan Teorell was formerly at Lund, and I have no documented tie to him beyond that. I have co-authored with the political scientist Johannes Lindvall and Alexandra Cermeño, and no candidate is connected to either. These are disclosed and not adjudicated. I do not claim independent verification of any source.
